hero.h1: Directive 8020 Actress & Cast — Who Plays Who on the Cassiopeia
hero.intro: Lashana Lynch leads the crew. Here's every actor, every role, and what you've seen them in before.

intro: If you just finished a scene and thought “wait, I know that voice,” you're not crazy. The **Directive 8020 actress** lineup pulls from some serious talent — Marvel veterans, British TV staples, and a few faces that Supermassive fans will recognize from previous Dark Pictures entries. Let's go through the full cast so you know exactly who's behind every crew member on the Cassiopeia.

sections.heading: Lashana Lynch as Brooke Osmond — The Lead

blocks.text: Let's start with the obvious one. Lashana Lynch plays **Brooke Osmond**, the co-pilot of the Cassiopeia and the character you'll spend the most time controlling. If she looks familiar, it's because Lynch has been everywhere lately — she played Maria Rambeau in *Captain Marvel* and took over the 007 title in *No Time to Die*. She also had a standout role in *The Woman King*.

Osmond is the moral center of Directive 8020, and Lynch plays her with a grounded intensity that sells the horror without ever tipping into melodrama. She's easily the strongest performance in the game, which is exactly what you want from your lead when the story asks you to make genuinely tough calls about who lives and who dies.

sections.heading: Danny Sapani as Commander Stafford — The Captain

blocks.text: Danny Sapani voices **Commander Stafford**, the commanding officer of the Cassiopeia. Sapani is one of those “oh, that guy” actors — you've definitely seen him in *Black Panther* (he played M'Kathu, the Border Tribe leader), *Harlots*, and *Penny Dreadful*. His voice carries the kind of weary authority that makes Stafford feel like a real leader who's been doing this job for way too long.
Stafford has some of the best scenes in the game, especially in Episode 6 during the two-Eisele standoff and in Episode 5 when his leadership cracks. Sapani absolutely delivers in those moments.

sections.heading: The Directive 8020 Actress Behind Dr. Eisele

blocks.text: Dr. Eisele is arguably the most important character in the game — she's central to the clone plotline, the true ending, and the biggest choice you'll make across all eight episodes. The actress playing her brings a careful, scientific detachment to the role that makes it genuinely hard to tell whether you're talking to the real Eisele or the mimic in Episode 6 — which is exactly the point.

Supermassive Games has not publicly credited the actress behind Eisele with as much fanfare as Lynch or Sapani, which has led to a fair amount of discussion in the community. If you're digging for the name, it may be listed in the full credits sequence after completing the game.

sections.heading: The Supporting Crew — Cernan, Cooper, Carter & Simms

blocks.text: The rest of the Directive 8020 cast fills out the Cassiopeia's crew with solid performances across the board. Josef Cernan becomes playable for the first time in Episode 3, and his actor brings a younger, more uncertain energy that contrasts nicely with Stafford's stoicism. Cooper is resourceful and gets some of the game's best one-liners, while Carter and Simms — despite having scripted deaths you can't prevent — both get enough screen time in Episode 1 to make their losses feel meaningful.

One thing worth noting: the Dark Pictures Anthology has a history of using recognizable face models alongside professional voice actors, so some characters may look like someone you know even if a different actor provided the performance. Supermassive has used this dual-casting approach since *Until Dawn*, and Directive 8020 continues the tradition.

sections.heading: How the Cast Compares to Previous Dark Pictures Games

blocks.text: Directive 8020 features a smaller core cast than some previous entries. *House of Ashes* had five leads plus supporting NPCs with big names. *The Devil in Me* similarly pulled recognizable talent. Directive 8020 keeps things tighter — seven total crew members, five playable, with the acting budget clearly concentrated on Lynch and Sapani. The result is a more focused story where the performances carry more weight because there are fewer characters competing for your attention.
If you're coming to this game as a fan of the actors first and the horror second, you'll be happy. Lynch in particular gives one of the best performances in the entire anthology.

items.q: Q: Who is the main Directive 8020 actress playing Osmond?
items.a: Lashana Lynch plays Brooke Osmond, the co-pilot and primary protagonist. You may know her from *No Time to Die*, *Captain Marvel*, or *The Woman King*.

items.q: Q: Are any of the Directive 8020 cast members from previous Dark Pictures games?
items.a: Supermassive frequently reuses face models and occasionally voice actors across the anthology. Check the full credits after beating the game to compare with earlier titles.

items.q: Q: Is the Directive 8020 actress for Eisele publicly confirmed?
items.a: While Lashana Lynch and Danny Sapani received top billing in pre-release marketing, the full credited cast — including Eisele's actress — appears in the game's end credits sequence.
